title: I Let the Lute-Pegbox Clock Catch the Mentor Who Camped My Numbered Frets

parts.text: I stepped into the pegbox room at 4:11 p.m. and mentor Cosimo was already using numbered gear. The board said: ONE LUTE. SIXTY MINUTES. FRETS STAY WITH THE SLOT. I was thirty-three, studio secretary, holding a checkout that listed our numbered frets. Cosimo shrugged. "Mentors are the pegbox." I photographed the board, the booking, and his leftover gut on my numbered frets. Then I asked for the fret log. At 4:19 the desk pinged why Cosimo's name was on my gut. I kept my voice indoor and let the timestamp talk. A paper policy is only paper until someone treats it like a clock.
parts.cliffhanger_hint: The desk can see Cosimo's leftover gut on my numbered frets.

social.video_title: He camped my numbered lute frets on my slot — Part 1/2
social.description: Pegbox room, leftover gut, a sixty-minute clock he posted. I logged the frets. Would you have asked for the fret log?

parts.text: Cosimo called it tying until the desk asked for the photo. I printed the ticket, the board, and the gut still. The frets went back to my numbered slot. Cosimo ran a slot of his own and told the next mentor atmosphere was always about optics. Optics is a word people use when a booking exists. Policy now has a second line: MENTORS ARE NOT THE PEGBOX. I keep my frets in a labeled coil. Cosimo brown-bags his tying. The pegbox room finally looks like a slot, not a loan. The rule looks ordinary now, which is the whole point.

social.video_title: Mentors are not the pegbox — Part 2/2
social.description: Fret log, numbered frets, and a second line on the board. Was tying ever my gut?
